question_variants: how long have you been open
entries.answer_spoken: Rosa Ibáñez opened Thimbleberry Bakehouse in 2011 in a former hardware store on Thimbleberry Street, after selling sourdough at a Saturday farmers market from 2008.
entries.answer_card: Rosa Ibáñez learned to bake in her grandmother's kitchen in Tucson, Arizona, then spent five years baking bread overnight for Portland restaurants. In 2008 she started selling sourdough at a Saturday farmers market, and in 2011 she opened Thimbleberry Bakehouse in a former hardware store on SE Thimbleberry Street. The bakery has one deck oven, one decorating bench and a team of nine.

evidence.quote: Thimbleberry Bakehouse opened in 2011 in a former hardware store on SE Thimbleberry Street, and the old shelving still holds our bread today.
in 2008 she started selling sourdough from a folding table at a Saturday farmers market.
Rosa Ibáñez learned to bake in her grandmother's kitchen in Tucson, Arizona
After moving to Portland she spent five years baking bread overnight for restaurants
We're still small on purpose: one deck oven, one decorating bench and a team of nine people who mostly start work before sunrise.

entries.answer_spoken: Rosa owns the bakery and plans every custom cake, and you'll usually find her at the counter on weekends. Teo is the head bread baker, and Maren decorates the cakes.

evidence.quote: Rosa Owner Plans every custom cake and reviews large orders herself. You'll usually find her at the counter on weekends.

question_variants: where do your ingredients come from
